businessRules.rule: A verification is scheduled and a list of assets is drawn for the room, person or department being checked.
Somebody other than the custodian confirms each asset is present and records its condition. A custodian verifying their own assets is confirming their own account of them, which is not a check.

Anything missing, moved, borrowed and not returned, or broken and quietly disposed of is recorded as an exception. The four are named separately because each is a different problem needing a different correction.

Each exception is resolved with an approved correction — a reassignment, a maintenance record or a disposal — and the reason is recorded. An exception noted and not resolved is the register drifting again.
A register nobody checks against reality is a list rather than a record, which is why this is not optional. It is scheduled and taken periodically, as the stock count is for stock.
An asset in scope that was not checked is reported as unchecked rather than as present. Unchecked and present mean different things.
The verification does not change the register by itself. The correction does, and only once approved.
Repeated exceptions on the same asset, or against the same custodian, are visible together. An asset missing at every verification is not an accident.
A verification is never deleted, and neither is an exception. The record of what was not where it should have been is the point.
A verification may cover a whole campus, a department, a room or one person's assets. The scope is chosen when it is scheduled.

transitions.condition: Every asset in scope is checked or reported unchecked (BR-6).

The correction is approved and applied (BR-7).
Returned with a reason. The register is unchanged.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Assets → Asset verifications → Schedule a verification
basicFlow.userAction: Schedules the verification and chooses the scope — a room, a person, a department or a campus.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Draws the list of assets expected in that scope.

basicFlow.userAction: Takes the verification, being somebody other than the custodian of what is being checked.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses where the verifier is the custodian of the assets in scope.

basicFlow.navigation: Take the verification → Mark present → Record the condition
basicFlow.userAction: Confirms each asset is present and records the condition it was found in.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records each line, and reports an asset not checked as unchecked rather than as present.

basicFlow.navigation: Take the verification → Raise an exception
basicFlow.userAction: Records anything missing, moved, borrowed and not returned, or broken and quietly disposed of.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the exception by type, since each is a different problem needing a different correction.

basicFlow.navigation: Exceptions → Reassign, Record maintenance, or Raise a disposal
basicFlow.userAction: Proposes the correction that resolves each exception, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds it for approval. The verification does not change the register by itself.
Applies the reassignment, maintenance record or disposal, and the register changes now.
Completes the verification once every exception is resolved, and shows repeated exceptions on the same asset or custodian together.

alternateFlows.condition: The custodian attempts to verify their own assets
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. A custodian verifying their own is confirming their own account of them (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: An asset is somewhere other than where the register says
alternateFlows.navigation: Take the verification → Raise an exception → Moved
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded as moved and resolved by a reassignment, which is a different correction from a missing asset (BR-3, BR-4).

alternateFlows.navigation: Take the verification → Raise an exception → Broken and quietly disposed of
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is resolved by a maintenance record or a disposal, according to what happened (BR-3, BR-4).
alternateFlows.function: raiseVerificationException(verificationId, assetId, 'Broken and quietly disposed of', note)

alternateFlows.condition: An asset was borrowed and not returned
alternateFlows.navigation: Take the verification → Raise an exception → Borrowed and not returned
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is recorded against whoever has it and resolved by a reassignment (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept a correction
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns and the register is unchanged. The exception stays outstanding (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: An asset in scope was not checked
alternateFlows.navigation: Take the verification → Not yet checked
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is reported as unchecked, since unchecked and present mean different things (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The same asset is an exception at every verification
alternateFlows.behaviour: The exceptions are visible together, since an asset missing at every verification is not an accident (BR-8).

departures.aspect: The verifier is never the custodian
departures.requirement: There is no route by which somebody verifies assets assigned to themselves. A custodian verifying their own is confirming their own account of them.
No verification entry changes the register. Only an approved correction does.
A verification cannot complete while any exception is unresolved. An exception noted and not resolved is the register drifting again.
An asset in scope that was not checked is reported as unchecked everywhere, and is never treated as found.
Verifications and their exceptions are retained 7 years, since they explain every change the register cannot otherwise account for.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
